a.summary: The new `///` block sits below the commented-out deprecation lines, so uncommenting them — the stated in-file TODO — silently drops the entire block from the generated javadoc.
a.failure_scenario: The file's TODO reads "deprecate once v1 transactions are active on mainnet". When a maintainer actions it and uncomments lines 433-434, the source becomes `/// @deprecated ...` / `@Deprecated` / `/// With one or more lookup tables, ...` / `static Transaction createTx(...)`. javac 25 with -Xlint:all then reports `warning: [dangling-doc-comments] documentation comment is not attached to any declaration` pointing at the NEW block, and only the `@deprecated` line binds to the method. The build still succeeds, so the in-place-mutation warning disappears from the published javadoc for 25.12.0+ with nothing but a lint warning to notice it — exactly when the deprecation makes consumers more likely to be reading the doc.

b.summary: The zero-table clause is literally true but presents a destructive path as a benign rebuild: it discards the caller's fee-payer designation and every account not referenced by an instruction, and downgrades the result to a legacy message.
b.failure_scenario: A caller resolves lookup tables at runtime and gets none back, so tableAccountMetas is a zero-length array (e.g. from LookupTableAccountMeta.createMetas(emptyCollection)). They call Transaction.createTx(List.of(memoIx), len, sortV0Accounts(merged), metas) where `merged` was built with a separate fee payer via AccountMeta.createFeePayer(payer) that no instruction references. Line 445 dispatches to createTx(instructions), which is createTx((AccountMeta) null, instructions) — mergeAccounts is called with a null fee payer (TransactionRecord.java:94-96), so the payer is never merged in. The returned transaction omits the payer from the account list entirely, numRequiredSignatures is 0, sigLen is 1, and TransactionRecord.feePayer is null. The caller ships an unsignable transaction with no signature slot, or NPEs on tx.feePayer(). The doc's "rebuilds from instructions" gives no hint that the account set shrinks. The Map-taking sibling at line 421 does not have this behaviour: with an empty array it calls createTx(instructions, serializedInstructionLength, sortLegacyAccounts(mergedAccounts)) and keeps every merged account including the fee payer.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
